resolutions.researcher_notes: PNGRB's NGPL MIS Report (edition 'as on 31.12.2025') lists PL Unique ID 21.01.NGPL 'Jaigarh - Dabhol' (entity WCPL) under the table header 'Operational Tie-in connectivity', with Operating Length 60.00 of 60.00 km Authorised Length -- i.e. mechanically complete and classified by the regulator as operational. url_verifier gives a false negative on this PDF (documented large-PDF text-extraction gotcha); I fetched it directly with curl and confirmed the row by hand with pdftotext -layout (verifier does confirm live 200 status). Independently, offshore-technology.com's trade-press project page describes the completed 60km tie-in linking the (now-inaugurated, May 2018 per Times of India) Jaigarh LNG terminal into GAIL's operating DUDPL/DBPL transmission grid. CAVEAT (not a value change): a separate concern about the terminal's own supply reliability (its FSRU arrived a year late and its charter was later terminated -- see Delay [ref]) means actual gas THROUGHPUT is unverified, but GEM's Status field tracks pipeline build/operational-lifecycle state, which both sources confirm as complete and in service.

PNGRB's register (NGPL = Natural Gas Pipeline) itself is fuel-scoped: 'Jaigarh - Dabhol' is listed in the natural-gas pipeline inventory (confirmed locally via pdftotext, verifier false-negative caveat as above). offshore-technology.com describes the line carrying regasified LNG (natural gas) from the Jaigarh terminal into GAIL's natural-gas transmission networks. Two independent sources agree Fuel = Gas.

PNGRB's NGPL report structurally separates transmission-grade Natural Gas Pipelines (this report, incl. the Tie-in connectivity table this row sits in) from City/Local Natural Gas Distribution Networks (a distinct CGD authorisation track, reported separately) -- so inclusion in the NGPL register itself is evidence against a distribution classification. Directly on point, offshore-technology.com states the 60km tie-in 'will link the terminal to two natural gas pipeline networks on the western coast of India, namely Dahej-Uran-Dabhol-Panvel (DUDPL) and Dabhol-Bangalore (DBPL)... owned and operated by GAIL' -- i.e. a high-pressure tie-in feeding directly into GAIL's transmission grid, not a gathering or local-distribution line. Two independent sources support PipelineType = transmission.

Could not confirm StartYear1=2021 as an actual first-gas/commissioning year. The only 2021 figure I can find is nsenergybusiness.com's project page listing 'Expected Commissioning March 2021' for the Jaigarh LNG terminal (the pipeline's sole gas source) -- a pre-completion PROJECTION, not a confirmed outcome, and per this batch's guidance an authorisation/target date should not support a StartYear. The evidence actually points the other way: offshore-energy.biz reports the terminal's only FSRU (Hoegh Giant) did not arrive until 1 March 2022, a full year after that target, and two LNGPrime articles report Hoegh LNG terminated the FSRU charter in April 2022 ('the charterer's default of the contractual terms') and withdrew the vessel from India, with no confirmed permanent replacement found since. PNGRB's own tie-in table (confirmed via pdftotext) shows only Authorised/Operating length, no commissioning date, so it cannot corroborate 2021 either. I found no first-gas date for the pipeline itself, actual or otherwise, so I am not proposing a corrected value -- only flagging that 2021 looks like the terminal's original target carried onto the pipeline row rather than a confirmed outcome. This routes to a status-review pass, not this ref-sweep.

Delayed=yes/DelayType=confirmed is well supported even though I could not confirm StartYear1 itself (see Start [ref]). nsenergybusiness.com's project page lists 'Expected Commissioning March 2021' for the Jaigarh terminal that this tie-in exclusively serves; offshore-energy.biz independently reports the terminal's only FSRU (Hoegh Giant) arrived just 1 March 2022 -- a full year past that target -- 'ahead of its commissioning in the coming weeks'; and LNG Prime independently reports Hoegh LNG terminated that FSRU's charter in April 2022 over the charterer's default. Three independent sources establish a confirmed, multi-year slip against the project's own original schedule.

PNGRB's NGPL MIS Report ('as on 31.12.2025') lists the Jaigarh-Dabhol (WCPL) row's Authorised/Design Capacity as 29.00 MMSCMD, exact match to GEM's Capacity=29.00/CapacityUnits=MMSCMD -- confirmed by hand with pdftotext -layout after url_verifier's documented large-PDF false negative (verifier does confirm the URL is live, 200). Independently, offshore-technology.com states 'the nominal gas sent out from the terminal will be up to 29 million standard cubic metres per day (Mscmpd)' -- MMSCMD and Mscmpd are the same unit, million standard cubic metres per day, just abbreviated differently. Two independent sources, regulator + trade press, agree exactly.

PNGRB's NGPL MIS Report lists the Jaigarh-Dabhol (WCPL) row's Authorised Length as 60 km and Operating Length as 60.00 km (fully built) -- exact match to GEM's LengthKnown=60.00/LengthKnownUnits=km; confirmed by hand via pdftotext -layout (verifier false-negative caveat as above, live 200 confirmed). Independently, offshore-technology.com states 'PNGRB authorised H-Energy Gateway to build and operate a 60km tie-in pipeline from Jaigarh port to Dabhol in May 2015' and 'the engineering, procurement, construction, and maintenance contract for the 60km tie-in pipeline was awarded to Engineers India.' Two independent sources agree exactly on 60 km.

PNGRB's NGPL register names the row '21.01.NGPL Jaigarh - Dabhol', States traversed 'Maharashtra' (confirmed by hand via pdftotext, verifier false-negative caveat as above). offshore-technology.com states 'PNGRB authorised H-Energy Gateway to build and operate a 60km tie-in pipeline from Jaigarh port to Dabhol' -- matching GEM's StartLocation=Jaigarh LNG Terminal/EndLocation=Dabhol/State=Maharashtra exactly. Times of India independently corroborates the Jaigarh LNG terminal itself as the pipeline's origin point (H-Energy's FSRU-based terminal, inaugurated May 2018). Two-to-three independent sources confirm the endpoints.

PNGRB's entity-code legend spells out 'WCPL Western Concessions Private Limited' and the Jaigarh-Dabhol row's entity code is WCPL, confirmed by hand via pdftotext -layout on the current (Dec-2025) edition -- so this ownership is still current, not stale. Independently, Oil & Gas Journal states 'H-Energy, through its wholly owned subsidiary Western Concessions Private Ltd., has entered into a binding commitment with Hoegh LNG Holdings Ltd.' -- naming the exact legal entity as H-Energy's project subsidiary for this facility. Two independent sources (regulator + trade press) agree exactly with GEM's Owner1='Western Concessions Private Ltd' at 100%.
